scenes.heading: Scheduling
scenes.narration: Scheduling controls when pipelines run, from simple daily jobs to complex data-driven triggers.

scenes.heading: Ways to schedule work
bullets: Cron expressions for fixed clock times.
Data-aware triggers when a dataset updates.
scenes.narration: Cron expressions pin jobs to precise clock times, like six every morning. Interval schedules run work at a steady cadence such as hourly. Data-aware scheduling fires a pipeline the moment an upstream dataset updates, and some runs are triggered manually or by outside events.

scenes.heading: Backfilling and catchup
scenes.narration: A schedule combined with a start date defines a series of intervals, each becoming its own run. If the scheduler was off, it can backfill the missed intervals to fill the gap. When history is not needed, disabling catchup tells it to skip straight to the present.

scenes.heading: Time-based vs data-driven

left.title: Time-based
points: May process stale or missing data

scenes.narration: Time-based schedules are predictable but can fire before data arrives or after it went stale. Data-driven scheduling instead waits for the actual dataset update, so pipelines run exactly when there is fresh work. Modern platforms increasingly favor data awareness to cut wasted and premature runs.

scenes.text: Scheduling ranges from fixed cron times to data-driven triggers, and choosing well keeps runs timely without processing stale or missing data.
scenes.narration: Prefer data-aware triggers when freshness matters, so pipelines wake up precisely when their inputs are ready.
